content.text:
Question 1 (10 marks)
How have Pina Bausch's choreographic practices contributed to her being recognised as a seminal artist?
In your response, provide specific examples from her works.
OR
How have Ohad Naharin's choreographic practices contributed to him being recognised as a seminal artist?
In your response, provide specific examples from his works.

items: Pina Bausch: used improvisation and collaboration with dancers, establishing mutual trust by encouraging individualism in the choreography.
Played with conventional and non-conventional eg switching gender roles; transformed dance from the balletic world to the raw contemporary world incorporating body percussion and vocals eg Fritz.
Tanztheater combining dance and theatre; brought dance, theatre and German expressionism together, influenced by Kurt Jooss and Rudolph von Laban.
Experimenting with new techniques, breaking new ground; reworking original works eg Rite of Spring, Le Sacre du Printemps; other choreographers continue to take inspiration from her works.
Explores the power of relationships.
Ohad Naharin: always has a clear social and political conscience, but dances are not meant to be political; more interested in texture and multi-layered movement than storytelling.
Developed a new movement vocabulary relying on concepts and abstract interpretation; Gaga language emphasised exploration of sensation and availability for free movement.
Gaga presents as a movement language rather than technique; sensed where the body is in space without mirrors - interested in the 'how' not the 'what'.
Provided a framework for discovering and strengthening the body; choreographed with access for all to dance eg disabled; created Batsheva Dance Company.
Increasing use of technology eg computer coding and the internet; globalisation with wider audiences; collaborative process.

content.text:
Question 2 (10 marks)
Twyla Tharp reinvented dance to reflect a changing world.
Explain this statement in relation to the works of Twyla Tharp from the 1960s-1980s.
In your response, provide specific examples from her works.
OR
Akram Khan reinvented dance to reflect a changing world.
Explain this statement in relation to the works of Akram Khan from the 1990s-present.
In your response, provide specific examples from his works.

items: Twyla Tharp: major events of the 1960s-1980s eg JFK assassination, civil rights movements, Vietnam War, women's rights, protest movements, Apollo 11, the Cold War.
America becoming a superpower - postwar affluence; changing nature of music eg protest music, Beatles, Woodstock; technological development/revolution; pop art and popular culture.
Postmodernists challenged the boundaries of the modern era - time of experimental dance with no rules or boundaries; emergence of the Broadway musical as an artform.

Eclectic dance style drawing on a broad variety of styles in ballet, jazz, pedestrian, postmodern and break dance (In The Upper Room 1986, The Catherine Wheel 1981); pedestrian style connected with ballet, dance and film (Hair 1979, Ragtime 1981).
Choreographed for dance on television; worked on Broadway; created public credibility for use of popular music (Deuce Coupe 1973); collaboration with important ballet dancers eg Baryshnikov.
Akram Khan: emergence of issues surrounding race, multiculturalism, sexuality and economics; technology and the internet - globalisation, environmental awareness; aftermath of the Cold War.
Conflict in the Middle East, emergence of terrorism; development of contemporary dance companies merging ballet, cultural and modern contemporary influences.
Dance becoming minimalistic and pedestrian - incorporating text, speech and gesture; emotional effects of migration; connections to his culture and non-western cultures.
Use of traditional stories, movements and characters explored in modern ways; created a diverse movement vocabulary fusing Indian Kathak and contemporary.
Collaboration with other artists eg Anthony Gormley, Anish Kapoor, Sylvie Guillem; broadened audience awareness and acceptance; broke ground in non-traditional theatre spaces.

content.text:
Question 3 (20 marks)
Explain how Mats Ek uses dance and theatrical elements to explore the emotions of everyday situations.
In your response, provide specific examples from Appartement.

items: Dance elements: pedestrian movement layered with dynamics to create emotion; fusion of ballet, diverse contemporary and acting genres; signature movements including flexed feet and hands, demi and grand plies, lunges, contractions to show torso movements.
Unique use of space, time and dynamics; movement chosen for expression/meaning not purely aesthetics - often angular, shaky, disturbing; strongly controlled by dancers showing core use.
Theatrical elements: costumes, props, set/staging, lighting, music (live band), voice.
Emotions/everyday situations: staging symbolised by furniture - toilet, armchair, stove, door and pedestrian crossing (lighting); uses tragedy and humour in interpretation of human situations.
Importance of characters and relationships in creating movement expressing subtle emotions; human nature of being 'close yet separate' through intimacy, arguments, love, anger, feelings, actions.
Mats Ek's work said to be 'emotion made motion', both thrilling and unsettling; internationally acclaimed for shifting between dance and theatre.
Influences and background: father acclaimed actor, mother dancer/choreographer with Culberg ballet, drama education and German expressionism.
